Let $\ell\ge3$. The path graph $A_{\ell-1}$ has vertex set $\{0,1,\ldots,\ell-2\}$ and an edge between $a$ and $b$ exactly when $|a-b|=1$. For $n\ge0$ and a vertex $a$, let $\mathsf P_{n,a}$ be the set of sequences
$$
p=(a_0,a_1,\ldots,a_n)
$$
with $a_0=0$, $a_n=a$, each $a_j\in\{0,1,\ldots,\ell-2\}$, and $|a_j-a_{j-1}|=1$ for $1\le j\le n$. The set is finite; it may be empty. Let $V_{n,a}:=\mathbb C^{(\mathsf P_{n,a})}$ be the free complex vector space with basis $\{|p\rangle:p\in\mathsf P_{n,a}\}$, and put
$$
K_n:=\bigoplus_{a=0}^{\ell-2}\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V_{n,a}),
$$
omitting zero summands. For $p,q\in\mathsf P_{n,a}$, the matrix unit $E^{(n,a)}_{p,q}$ sends $|q\rangle$ to $|p\rangle$, sends every other path basis vector to zero, and is zero on every endpoint block other than $a$.

For $b\sim a$, write $pb=(a_0,\ldots,a_n,b)$ for the path obtained by appending $b$. Define the unital algebra map candidate $\iota_n:K_n\to K_{n+1}$ on matrix units by
$$
\iota_n(E^{(n,a)}_{p,q})=\sum_{b\sim a}E^{(n+1,b)}_{pb,qb},
$$
and extend it linearly. The next local theorem proves that these assignments are injective unital $*$-homomorphisms and gives the corresponding branching rule. This is an abstract path-space tower definition; it does not assert that a particular quotient of a Temperley–Lieb algebra is isomorphic to $K_n$.

derivations.claim: For any path $(a_0,\ldots,a_n,b)$ ending at $b$, its penultimate vertex $a$ is uniquely determined and satisfies $a\sim b$; deleting $b$ gives a unique prefix in $\mathsf P_{n,a}$. Conversely appending $b$ to any path in $\mathsf P_{n,a}$ with $a\sim b$ gives a path ending at $b$. Hence the set of paths ending at $b$ is the disjoint union of the appended path sets $\{pb:p\in\mathsf P_{n,a}\}$ over all such $a$. The basis vectors therefore split as the asserted direct sum, and $E^{(n,a)}_{p,q}$ acts on each appended block as the same matrix unit while acting by zero on the other predecessor blocks.

Take matrix units $X=E^{(n,a)}_{p,q}$ and $Y=E^{(n,c)}_{r,s}$. If $a\ne c$, then $XY=0$; in the product $\iota_n(X)\iota_n(Y)$ a nonzero matrix-unit product would require the middle path $qb$ to equal $rd$ for some $b\sim a$ and $d\sim c$, forcing both $q=r$ as length-$n$ paths and $a=c$, a contradiction. Thus the images multiply to zero.

If $a=c$, then $XY=\mathbf1_{q=r}E^{(n,a)}_{p,s}$. On multiplying the two sums in [F2], the only nonzero terms have the same appended vertex $b$ and equal middle path $qb=rb$, which is equivalent to $q=r$. The product is consequently $\mathbf1_{q=r}\sum_{b\sim a}E^{(n+1,b)}_{pb,sb}=\iota_n(XY)$. Adjoints are preserved because $\iota_n((E_{p,q}^{(n,a)})^*)=\sum_{b\sim a}E_{qb,pb}^{(n+1,b)}=\iota_n(E_{p,q}^{(n,a)})^*$. Bilinearity proves multiplicativity and $*$-preservation on all of $K_n$.

The identity of $K_n$ is $\sum_{a,p}E^{(n,a)}_{p,p}$. Its image is the sum of the diagonal units indexed by every one-step extension $pb$ of every length-$n$ path $p$; by step 1.1 each length-$(n+1)$ path occurs exactly once. This is the identity of $K_{n+1}$. For injectivity, every vertex $a$ has at least one neighbor in $A_{\ell-1}$, since $\ell\ge3$. For each source unit $E^{(n,a)}_{p,q}$ choose one neighbor $b$; the coordinate $E^{(n+1,b)}_{pb,qb}$ in its image determines the source unit uniquely by deleting the last vertex. Distinct source units therefore have disjoint image coordinates, so no nonzero linear combination maps to zero. Hence $\iota_n$ is a unital injective $*$-homomorphism and step 1.1 gives the multiplicity-one branching rule.
